key_insight: Putting trainable nonlinear functions on the connections of a physical neural network lets analogue hardware learn smooth continuous mappings efficiently, instead of using devices only as scalar weights.
engineering_relevance: This could enable ultra-low-power control and energy-management hardware, with a projected CMOS implementation around 30 microwatts and transfer across about 35,000 connections.
method: Implemented trainable nonlinear connection functions as analogue band-pass filters on field-programmable analogue arrays.
Compared performance across smooth regression/control tasks and classification-like decision boundaries.
Also evaluated transfer to hardware and a memristive simulation to isolate the effect of connection nonlinearity.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports strong parameter-efficiency gains on smooth targets such as robotic kinematics, continuous control, and photovoltaic maximum-power-point tracking, but not on classification-like boundaries.
watch_item: The advantage is task-dependent, so the approach may not improve all problems and requires careful hardware calibration/fidelity over large connection counts.
paper_title: Low-power analogue neural networks with trainable nonlinear connections for continuous control
